articles.title: German Economic Confidence Improves: ZEW
articles.expand: German economic confidence improved in October driven by declining oil prices and increased government expenditure, survey data from the Mannheim-based Centre for European Economic Research, or ZEW, showed Tuesday. The ZEW indicator of economic sentiment rose more-than-expected to 35.6 in October from 28.1 in the previous month. The score was seen at 28.8.

articles.title: Goldmans Sachs: France 2027 Outlook - FJElite
articles.expand: France’s economy has contracted by a cumulative 0.3% so far this year, with growth unlikely to recover meaningfully before next year’s elections. Tighter financial and lending conditions, political uncertainty and modest fiscal consolidation are weighing on activity. Growth is forecast at just 0.1% in 2027, the weakest outlook across developed markets covered, partly reflecting negative base effects. The fiscal position remains challenging despite expectations that a budget will be passed before year-end. Weak growth and elevated borrowing costs are expected to leave the deficit at 5.4% of GDP...

Uncertainty and stalemate in the Middle East are also weighing on market sentiment.

articles.title: Kuroda, once Japan’s great easer, says BOJ rates may need to rise above neutral
articles.expand: For Japanese rates and the yen, a call for above-neutral rates from the architect of Japan’s easing era adds weight to the hawkish tail of BOJ pricing. Most economists see a terminal rate near 1.75%, and talk of 2.5% now has a high-profile backer. Kuroda no longer sets policy, so the direct effect is limited. Still, his critique of the food tax cut puts the fiscal-monetary tension in sharp relief ahead of an expected December hike. Front-end JGB yields, with the two-year near 1.88%, are most exposed to any shift toward a higher peak. Oil matters here too. Kuroda explicitly links Japan’s inflat...

articles.title: RBA minutes: 6 members saw rates “not clearly sufficient”, 3 warned of sharper downturn
articles.expand: On balance the minutes lean hawkish, unsurpisngly. The majority’s view that 4.85% is “not clearly sufficient” sits awkwardly with market pricing that had all but ruled out further hikes, and it backs up Bullock’s comment this morning about upside risks. The minority’s warning of a sharper downturn sets a high bar for a December move, though. This week’s wage and jobs data, and the October CPI jump the staff flagged in advance, matter more than usual. For the Australian dollar, near 0.6730, the minutes are mildly supportive but unlikely to change the trend while policy diverges from the Fed. Th...

articles.title: RBA’s Bullock says inflation risks still skewed to upside ahead of 6-3 vote minutes
articles.expand: Bullock’s comment pushes back modestly against market pricing that has all but ruled out a December hike. It could offer the Australian dollar some support after it fell this week to its lowest level since late January. One line on a panel is unlikely to shift pricing on its own, so the minutes are the bigger test. Any sign that the majority on the board saw a real chance of further tightening would firm up the hawkish reading of Bullock’s remarks. If the minutes play up how close the vote was, front-end rates may decide the governor’s comment is a hedge, not a signal. - Minutes preview here: ...

articles.expand: Neither release is likely to move the New Zealand dollar much on its own. The Financial Stability Report assesses risk rather than signalling policy, and the food price data is only a small input into quarterly inflation. The RBNZ’s warning that recent cost pressures and higher interest rates could reverse the easing in domestic stress points in a cautious direction. Its list of global risks, from Middle East energy disruption to an AI valuation correction, reads like a list of the shocks that tend to hurt risk-sensitive currencies like the kiwi. --- Coming up later from neighbouring Australia...

articles.expand: Tiff Macklem announced that he will retire after his seven-year term ends in June 2027. He should have left much sooner. It continues to baffle me that no central banker paid the price for the disastrous covid inflation. In no other high-profile field in the world is incompetence tolerated to the extent it is in central banking. It's a field that's protected both by government independence and a culture that accepts failure. No one exemplified that more than Tiff Macklem and his performance during the pandemic. articles.title: BOJ’s Takata calls for nimble hikes after 1.5% bid, says neutral rate may top estimates
articles.expand: Takata’s speech is the clearest public argument yet for a faster BOJ hiking pace than markets assume. He rejects a fixed quarterly rhythm and argues for reaching the middle of the neutral range early, which puts a move beyond 1.5% within view. Because his views are his own and he has been outvoted, it doesn’t change December pricing by itself. But it supports the yen and adds upward pressure on front-end JGB yields, especially with USD/JPY near 160. His explicit link between real rate differentials and the currency also signals that BOJ hawks see rate hikes as a tool against yen weakness. On t...

articles.title: China factory output slows to 4.8% in October, retail sales up just 0.4% as demand sags
articles.expand: The data pushes in two directions for markets. Weak domestic demand and the investment slump support the case for more easing over time. But the view that no new stimulus will come this year limits any near-term “bad news is good news” rally in Chinese equities. The muted yuan reaction suggests the miss was largely expected. For commodities, slower factory output and the property slump are a headwind for iron ore and industrial metals. Softer Chinese activity also adds a mild drag on oil demand, against a supply backdrop still dominated by the Iran war. The Australian dollar is the most direct...

That limits any lasting yen weakness from the data, although USD/JPY near 160 remains in intervention territory. The risk lies in the board split some economists flagged. Further soft consumption data could give the doves more influence and push hike timing back, which would weigh on the yen and lift JGBs. Oil is the link in the middle. articles.title: ECB bond market intervention warning from Governor Knot. Can’t replace sound fiscal policy,
articles.expand: Knot’s line on fiscal discipline matters most for euro zone sovereign spreads, especially French bonds against German Bunds. Markets will read it as a reminder that ECB support would be conditional rather than open-ended. A president with that view could make investors less willing to bet on a full central bank backstop if French finances get worse, which risks wider spreads during periods of stress. On rates, his cautious, data-driven stance on energy-driven inflation is softer than the hike signals coming from more hawkish policymakers, so a Knot presidency would lean toward patience rather ...

articles.title: ECB’s Nagel says another rate hike ‘highly probable’ as energy prices push inflation
articles.expand: An explicit signal from the Bundesbank president that further tightening is likely should support the euro and push up short-dated euro zone yields, especially German two-year debt. Because he ties the risk directly to gas and electricity, euro zone rate pricing is now more sensitive to moves in energy markets, so a rise in oil or gas could feed quickly into ECB hike expectations. His comment that the economy has proved resilient also weakens the argument that growth worries will hold the ECB back, which leaves rate-sensitive European equities more exposed. --- Not only open mouths at the ECB:...

The flat employment reading and persistent cost-of-living complaints, however, point to slack that has not yet closed.
